sources.note: the sages: Janaka of Mithila will hold a sacrifice; come and see the wondrous bow (Ep07 setting)
the gods gave the bow; no god, gandharva, asura, rakshasa or man can string it (Ep07 teaser 1.31.9); mighty kings tested it and could not string it (1.31.10)
Vishvamitra takes leave of the forest deities and sets out north; a hundred carts of brahmavadins follow; the hermitage's deer and birds follow him
he turns the birds and beasts back; at sunset they camp on the bank of the Shona; Rama asks: what land is this, rich with forests?
urged by Rama, the sage tells the whole story of that land among the sages
Kusha and his four sons found cities; Kushanabha founds Mahodaya and fathers a hundred daughters by Ghritachi
Vayu sees them: I desire you all, you will be my wives; leave the human state, gain long life, unfading youth, immortality

they laugh off his words; we could topple you from your place, but we guard our tapas; never will we slight our truthful father and choose for ourselves; whoever our father gives us to will be our husband
Vayu, enraged, enters all their limbs and breaks them; they return weeping; the king asks who made them all hunchbacked (कुब्जाः)
the daughters tell their father: we are not free to choose; ask our father; for saying this, Vayu struck us hard

sources.edition: vulgate (sa.wikisource; valmikiramayan.net labels the card lines 1.33.8b–9a)
sources.note: the king: you have forgiven, as the forgiving do; forgiveness is charity, truth, sacrifice, glory, dharma; on forgiveness the world stands (verse card 1.33.8–9)
Brahmadatta, king of Kampilya; Kushanabha gives him the hundred daughters; at the mere touch of his hand they are unbent and free of pain
Gadhi is born to Kushanabha; the sage: that Gadhi is my father, I am Kaushika of Kusha's line
teaser verse 1.34.8: his elder sister Satyavati, given to Richika, followed her husband bodily to heaven and flowed forth as the great river Kaushiki

learnings.how: Partly applied. The stakes are in the hook itself (a hundred princesses refuse a god). The shape is the 45 s default trimmed toward 35 s, not the 35 s anecdote shape: the story needs offer, refusal, curse, the father's verdict and the cure, plus the Ep07 payoff and the teaser. In en the curse lands at about 27–31 s, the verse card follows, and the main loop closes at the healing by about 87% of runtime.

Applied. Hooks are 2.5–2.9 s in every language with the stakes in the first sentence; gu is written natively short (ના પાડી), not translated. Frame 0 is the hook image (princesses under the wind spiral), to be drawn ≥70% by the engine (O5).
Applied. Estimates sit in the lower-middle of 35–55 s (see the lint line above), and gu/te/mr stay at or under 53 s (narration rewrite for flow, 2026-11-17; the owner asked for flow over brevity).

Applied on screen. Scene 10 carries the ≤6-word engagement line as its title card (en 'What holds up the world?'), answered in the text by the verse card just before it (forgiveness, 1.33.8–9). It is not spoken, because gu/te/mr have no seconds to spare. The same line is suggested as the pinned comment so shares/reach can be compared next time.
